title: Kernel Methods & the Kernel Trick
interviewAnswer: Kernel methods replace an explicit nonlinear feature map with a kernel that computes inner products in that feature space, enabling algorithms such as SVMs to learn nonlinear boundaries without materializing all transformed features.
why: Kernels are a classic bridge between linear methods and nonlinear function spaces.
intuition: If a linear separator fails in original coordinates, map inputs into richer features—but compute only pairwise inner products through a kernel.
deepDive: A valid kernel corresponds to an inner product in some feature space. The RBF kernel creates a very rich space controlled by gamma/bandwidth; regularization still controls effective complexity.
commonMistakes: Saying kernels simply “add dimensions” with no mathematical constraint.
Using RBF gamma without scaling/tuning features.
followUps: Why do kernel methods scale poorly with n?
production: Kernel matrices can be O(n²) memory/time; use approximations or other models at large scale.
workedExample: Two concentric classes can become separable under a suitable nonlinear kernel even though no straight boundary works in input space.
